# Portfolio 4: NoSQL and Advanced Data Models

**Case study:** Konga, a simulated multi-seller marketplace (see the root README). All data is synthetic and generated by `src/00_generate_data.mjs` (2,000 products, 2,000 customers, about 14,900 purchases, fixed random seed).

This portfolio starts from [Portfolio 1’s relational design](../portfolio-1-database-design/docs/design-report.md) and asks whether another model makes some tasks easier. Orders, payments and stock remain in PostgreSQL. The experiments explore documents for product attributes, Redis for application state and caching, and a graph model for recommendations.

## Evidence checklist

The checklist separates the prepared scripts from the results that still need to be collected. Mark an experiment complete after running it and saving its output.
- [ ] Document model (FerretDB, MongoDB protocol): [`src/01_document_ferretdb.mjs`](src/01_document_ferretdb.mjs) -> `evidence/01-document-model-output.txt`
- [ ] Key-value model (Redis): [`src/02_keyvalue_redis.mjs`](src/02_keyvalue_redis.mjs) -> `evidence/02-keyvalue-output.txt`
- [ ] Graph model (LadybugDB, Cypher): [`src/03_graph_ladybug.mjs`](src/03_graph_ladybug.mjs) -> `evidence/03-graph-output.txt`
- [ ] Wide-column model: **design only, not run**: [`design/cassandra_shipment_events.cql`](design/cassandra_shipment_events.cql)
- [x] NoSQL model for the same case study: [`design/relational_to_nosql_mapping.md`](design/relational_to_nosql_mapping.md)
- [ ] Suitability against relational, NewSQL and BASE: [`docs/analysis.md`](docs/analysis.md) (complete the comparisons using the saved experiment output)

## Setup (macOS, Homebrew)
```bash
npm install                       # once, at the repository root
brew install redis                # key-value part
# Document part needs a MongoDB-protocol server. Either:
#  a) FerretDB 1.x (stores data in PostgreSQL): download the binary or run it with Docker, listening on 127.0.0.1:27017
#  b) real MongoDB (set MONGO_URI). Then describe MongoDB as the server used in the analysis.
```
FerretDB needs an empty PostgreSQL database named `ferretdb`: `createdb ferretdb`.

## How to run

Run from the repository root. Set the connection variables if your PostgreSQL is not on `localhost:5432` as your Mac user.
```bash
npm run p4:data                                   # writes data/products.json and data/purchases.csv

# 1. Document model (needs the FerretDB/MongoDB server running, and the konga_p1 database from Portfolio 1)
node portfolio-4-nosql/src/01_document_ferretdb.mjs 2>&1 | tee portfolio-4-nosql/evidence/01-document-model-output.txt

# 2. Key-value model (needs: redis-server --port 6380 --save "" --daemonize yes, and the Portfolio 2 database `konga` seeded)
REDIS_PORT=6380 node portfolio-4-nosql/src/02_keyvalue_redis.mjs 2>&1 | tee portfolio-4-nosql/evidence/02-keyvalue-output.txt

# 3. Graph model (needs the konga_p1 database)
node portfolio-4-nosql/src/03_graph_ladybug.mjs 2>&1 | tee portfolio-4-nosql/evidence/03-graph-output.txt
```
Create the `evidence/` folder first (`mkdir -p portfolio-4-nosql/evidence`). Variables: `KONGA_PG_HOST`, `KONGA_PG_PORT`, `KONGA_PG_USER`, `KONGA_P1_DB` (default `konga_p1`), `KONGA_DB` (default `konga`, the Portfolio 2 database), `MONGO_URI`, `REDIS_PORT`. The Redis durability test starts and kills its own temporary Redis servers on ports 6391 to 6393.

Scripts 01 and 03 create and drop their own scratch schemas (`nosql_cmp`, `graph_cmp`) inside `konga_p1`, so they do not touch your Portfolio 1 tables. Script 02 only reads from the Portfolio 2 database.

## How to interpret the results

- **FerretDB is not MongoDB.** It speaks the MongoDB protocol and stores data in PostgreSQL, and it may not implement every operator. Results for the document model describe the server you used.
- Timings come from one machine, so only large differences mean anything.
- The wide-column model is design only: no Cassandra server was run.

## Design choices and lessons learned

- I did not replace the relational design. Each model is explored for a particular need in the marketplace.
- The results summary is still pending. After running the scripts, compare correctness, response times and the extra work needed to operate each store before deciding which parts of the model should use it.

## Limitations

The dataset contains 2,000 synthetic products, and the document results depend on whether FerretDB or MongoDB is used. Cassandra is covered as a design exercise. There is no multi-node NoSQL test, so the discussion of partitioning, replication and CAP in [the analysis](docs/analysis.md) describes design choices rather than measured behaviour.
